title: How To Avoid Parent Complaints About Online Learning https://smartclassroommanagement.com/2020/05/09/avoid-parent-complaints-about-online-learning/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin argues that remote learning gives parents unprecedented visibility into every lesson and assignment, raising the risk of complaints, and offers five ways to preempt them by projecting professional authority. He advises against apologizing for assigned work, since apologies invite negotiation over its amount or content. He recommends keeping communication professional rather than overly familiar, since teachers who become too friendly with parents end up fielding more special requests. Instructions should be simple and clear enough to leave no room for interpretation, reducing the opportunities for complaint in the first place. When a complaint does arrive, he advises not taking it personally and sticking strictly to facts rather than over-explaining or negotiating. He closes by framing professionalism and confidence, not friendliness, as what earns parents' trust during a uniquely stressful and scrutinized period.
points: Avoid apologizing for assigned work, since apologies invite parents to negotiate its amount or content.
Keep communication professional rather than overly familiar; overly friendly teachers face more special requests.
Make instructions simple and clear enough to leave little room for interpretation or complaint.
When a complaint arrives, don't take it personally — listen, clarify once, and don't negotiate further.
Stick to facts when discussing behavior or performance with parents rather than over-explaining or offering unsolicited opinions.
